To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

doctors who were trained only in Western medicine (WMDs), had the highest use of mainstream Western medicine, followed by doctors trained in both Western medicine and Chinese medicine (WMD-CMDBs), while Chinese Medicine-trained doctors (CMD) had the lowest utilization.
the training background of doctors is significantly associated with their own use of WM and CAM and their relatives' utilization of WM and CAM.

doctors trained in Western medicine (WMDs), Chinese medicine (CMDs) and both (WMDs-CMDs) had a higher use of Western medicine (WM), traditional Chinese medicine (TCH) and WM and TCM, respectively, than the general population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of training on the utilization of mainstream WM and TCM among physicians.
the utilization of WM and traditional medicine by physicians and their relatives and its relationship to training background.
the utilization of WM and CAM by physicians and their families.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the utilization of WM and CAM by both the doctors and their relatives is influenced by training background.
the training background of physicians does affect their own and their relatives' utilization of both WM and TCM, but the effect is not consistent and is not straightforward.
WMD-CMD physicians and their relatives had the highest utilization of TCM services, while WMDs and their relatives had a higher utilization of WM services.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the training background of doctors may influence their own use of WM and/or TCM services and that of their relatives.
the more the doctors are exposed to different training background, the less likely they are to use their own training background services.
the training background of physicians has a significant effect on their personal utilization of WM and CAM.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the training background of physicians may influence their own utilization of medical services and that of their relatives, and that this may be a factor in the observed disparities in utilization of Western medicine and traditional Chinese medicine.
the training background of a practitioner has a significant impact on his/her utilization of different medical disciplines.
the utilization of WM and CAM by both doctors and their relatives is associated with the training backgrounds of the doctors.
